summary: Ephemeral connection reset at edge during canary cutover caused silent fallback and pin inconsistency
description:
Issue summary:
During a scheduled canary cutover for redwood-v1-7b -> gpt-neoX-20b on 2026-02-17, a subset of tenant requests were routed to a fallback (legacy) variant despite an explicit model pin being asserted. The condition was silent (no 5xxs or obvious errors to the customer) but caused quality regressions for ~2% of requests for NimbleRetail during a 9-minute window.

Impact:
- NimbleRetail (dedicated) reported subtle output differences leading to two failed downstream QA checks and an automated rollback of their internal feature flag.
- Estimated affected traffic: 1.6k requests over 9 minutes (~2% of their traffic in us-east).
- No billing discrepancy observed; issue is correctness/consistency.

Timeline (abridged):
- 2026-02-17 09:05 UTC: Canary weight adjustment from 5% -> 20% begins.
- 2026-02-17 09:06 UTC: Edge-proxy detected brief connection reset to orchestrator (socket RST).
- 2026-02-17 09:06-09:15 UTC: Intermittent tenant requests returned legacy variant outputs despite edge showing pin claim for new model.
- 2026-02-17 10:00 UTC: Customer reported anomalies to Support.
- 2026-02-17 10:20 UTC: Support escalated to SRE and Serving Runtime.
- 2026-02-17 15:00 UTC: Hotfix deployed to edge-proxy to increase handshake retry window and add durable pin commit ACKs.
- 2026-02-17 16:45 UTC: Incident marked Resolved.

Environment:
- prod - us-east (edge cluster e-us-3, orchestrator set ork-us-east-02)
- Tenant: nimbleretail-prod on Dedicated pool D-42

Steps to reproduce (best-effort):
1) Trigger a controlled canary weight increase for tenant with pin-in-place.
2) Inject a short TCP RST between edge instance and orchestrator during snapshot commit.
3) Observe: edge logs show local pin claim; orchestrator lacks the commit; requests routed to fallback variant when orchestrator responds from older snapshot.

Observed behavior:
- Edge returned streaming responses with headers X-Model: redwood-v1-7b (claimed pin), but the content matched legacy variant outputs (gpt-neoX-20b not applied).
- No 5xxs; observability metrics did not flag errors because both edge and orchestrator responded successfully, just with mismatched snapshots.

Hypothesis:
- A connection reset during the snapshot commit window caused a one-way commit visibility problem. Edge persisted a local pin state and continued serving until it reconciled with the control plane. Meanwhile the orchestrator resumed serving from the previous snapshot, causing silent, per-request model divergence (edge-level pin vs orchestra-level routing).

Immediate mitigation performed:
- Temporarily paused canary weight growth and rolled the canary back to 5% for NimbleRetail.
- Deployed edge-proxy hotfix (PR #1987) that: increases handshake retry/backoff during pin commit and marks pin commits as needing ACK from orchestrator before edge promotes local claim for >30s.
- Added alert rule on pin-claim/commit-ack latency (>500ms) for dedicated tenants.

Longer-term actions (tracked separately):
- Ensure persistent commit ACKs are recorded in control-plane audit logs and surfaced to metrics.
- Add end-to-end snapshot consistency check during canary transitions (control plane, orchestrator, edge).
- Update runbook for canary weight increases to include preflight snapshot sync verification for dedicated tenants.

Evidence and logs (excerpts):
- edge-proxy log (e-us-3) 2026-02-17T09:06:12Z: "WARN pin-commit: local-claim set for tenant=nimbleretail, snapshot=2026-02-17T09:05:55Z, awaiting commit-ack"
- edge-proxy log (e-us-3) 2026-02-17T09:06:12Z: "ERROR conn reset to ork-us-east-02: write: connection reset by peer"
- orchestrator log (ork-us-east-02) 2026-02-17T09:06:13Z: "INFO serving snapshot snapshot=2026-02-16T22:00:00Z for tenant=nimbleretail"
- support transcript (customer): "We saw subtle changes in generated product descriptions that caused two items to fall out of QA — no obvious errors returned, just different wording."
investigation_notes: SRE reproduced the mismatch in staging by replaying the commit sequence with an injected RST. Trace showed edge state machine moved to 'claimed' on local commit but orchestrator never transitioned atomically due to lost commit packet. Control-plane retry logic allowed reconcilation but only after ~8 minutes when the next heartbeat triggered snapshot refresh. The hotfix forces the edge to stall promotion until ACK or a configured timeout—preventing silent divergence. We also confirmed similar races in a dedicated tenant when network blips are present and can be amplified by low socket backlog settings on kernel. Suggested kernel tweak and adjusted proxy connection pooling settings in the hotfix.
comments: 2026-02-17 10:25 UTC - Support (Maya Chen): Customer reports unexpected content differences during canary. Asked for request ids and sample outputs.
2026-02-17 11:05 UTC - SRE (Liam Patel): Reproduced locally in staging using a packet-drop RST during snapshot commit. Sharing reproduction script and logs in #support and linking PR later.
2026-02-17 13:40 UTC - Serving (Sofia Ruiz): Confirmed orchestrator did not commit snapshot; edge persisted local claim. Working on patch to require commit-ack before promotion for dedicated tenants.
2026-02-17 15:10 UTC - Deployment (Ethan Brooks): Hotfix rolled to e-us-3 and ork-us-east-02. Observability shows pin-ack latency metric populated; no further mismatches in the 2h post-deploy window.

2026-02-18 09:05 UTC - Customer (NimbleRetail - V. Kapoor): Appreciated quick response; requested a short postmortem and whether this could happen for multi-region cutovers. Asked to be on the early warning list for future canaries.

2026-02-24 16:30 UTC - Support (Maya Chen): Followed up with postmortem link and scheduled a 1:1 with NimbleRetail CS to review canary playbook. Customer accepted mitigation and no further incidents reported.

2026-03-01 12:00 UTC - SRE (Liam Patel): Added control-plane metric 'pin_commit_ack_rate' and a guardrail to block canary >25% weight unless snapshot consistency check passes for 3 continuous minutes.
root_cause: A transient TCP connection reset during the snapshot commit window caused the edge to record a local pin-claim without receiving an orchestrator commit acknowledgement. This produced a short window where edge and orchestrator served different snapshot versions, causing silent fallback-like behavior (content mismatch without HTTP errors).
resolution: Deployed edge-proxy change to require commit-ack from orchestrator before promoting local pin for production/dedicated tenants (PR #1987). Increased handshake retry/backoff and added pin commit ACK metrics and alerts. Updated canary runbook and added snapshot consistency gating for weight increases.
follow_up_actions: Add end-to-end commit-ack tracing across control plane, orchestrator, and edge
Integrate snapshot-consistency check into canary pipeline
Tune kernel socket backlog defaults for dedicated edge instances
Notify enterprise customers of pin-ack guardrails and offer opt-in early-warning notifications
notes_for_customers: We deployed a targeted fix and added monitoring to prevent recurrence. For dedicated customers running canaries, we now require snapshot-commit acknowledgment before the edge promotes a local pin — this prevents silent divergences even if short network blips occur. CS will coordinate a brief review of canary runbooks with NimbleRetail.
